text:
morgan: Heads up — nightly perf job started failing with GPU OOMs after the kernel-routing change landed. Repro on a 16k-seqlen workload (batch=4) when kv-cache warms up.

infra-bot: [job 3509876550] repro-run-alloc-probe finished: status=OOM on worker g4-12. Logs: https://ci/redwood/jobs/3509876550

sasha: I saw something similar in profiling yesterday. The allocator spikes when we switch kernels for long context; memory gets fragmented and expandable_segments tries to split a lot of small chunks.

lee: Can you paste the knob values used in the failing run? I want to see expandable_segments / max_split_size_mb / garbage_collection_threshold.

morgan: Sure — config snippet from the runner:```
allocator.knobs.expandable_segments = true
allocator.knobs.max_split_size_mb = 8
allocator.knobs.garbage_collection_threshold = 0.8
server.kv_cache.prewarm = true
server.batching.autoscale = true
```

anas: That max_split_size_mb=8 is tiny for 16k sequences — we'll create a lot of splits which increases fragmentation. Also gc threshold at 0.8 defers collection, so freeable slabs pile up.

sasha: Agreed. From the perf trace (sampling):
```
# simplified trace counts
alloc_large_chunk (attn kernel switch) x120
split_segment x840
gc_scan x3  (triggered late)
kv_cache_migrate x45
```
The hot path is kernel selection + kv_cache migrations causing many mid-sized frees/allocs.

morgan: Quick experiment: bump max_split_size_mb to 64 and lower gc threshold to 0.6 — will run now.

infra-bot: [job 3509876580] alloc-probe started with knobs: max_split=64, gc_thresh=0.6

lee: Also try temporarily toggling expandable_segments=false; that forces larger contiguous allocations and may help reuse buffers across kernel switch. Worth A/B.

morgan: Results from the run: no OOM, token throughput down ~6% but p99 latency improved on steady-state. Summary:
```
old: OOM @ step ~420
new(max_split=64,gc=0.6): no OOM, throughput -6%, p99 -12%
new(no-expando): no OOM, throughput -9%, p99 -4% (less variance)
```

anas: Interesting — disabling expandable_segments reduces fragmentation at cost of peak throughput. For our production SLOs, predictable p99 matters more.

sasha: Kernel selection still causes some small allocations during kv_cache handoff. We should prioritize buffer reuse in that hotpath — maybe keep a small dedicated workspace pool for kv-cache migrations.

lee: I'll sketch a small change: on kernel switch path, try to allocate from a "scratch buffer pool" sized to current sequence length distribution before hitting allocator split logic. If pool miss, fall back to normal. That should avoid churn.

morgan: +1. Also propose adding a targeted test in perf CI: long-context kv-warmup with various knob combos. We should catch regressions when we change kernels.

infra-bot: Created perf test: perf/kv-warmup-longctx in nightly matrix (refs #4532).

anas: For immediate mitigation, recommend default knob change in dedicated pools: max_split_size_mb=32 and garbage_collection_threshold=0.65, and set expandable_segments=true for regular workloads but false for long-kv warmup instances. Document tradeoffs.

lee: I'll open the PR to add the scratch pool and switch defaults for the dedicated tier. Assigning to @morgan to validate on canary.

morgan: Thanks — will validate tomorrow morning and post results here. If I see any regressions I'll roll back the knob default in config service. :thumbsup:

sasha: One more note: add allocator histograms to the runtime tracing (split counts, largest_free_chunk_over_time) so engineers can correlate kernel-rollouts with fragmentation.

morgan: Good call. I'll add a quick dashboard panel for that once the perf data lands.

lee: TL;DR — cause: kernel routing + kv-cache handoff produced lots of small splits; fixes: raise max_split_size_mb, lower gc threshold, add scratch pool, optionally disable expandable_segments for long-context lanes.

morgan: Closing thread for now — will update with canary numbers.
